rationale: This is a mechanical blend of two already-tested archive winners (Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value and Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value) that share an identical cash leg, so it is a re-weighting exercise whose result is largely predictable from the correlation of the two parents rather than a new mechanism.

The cash-provenance leg (cash net of recent liability expansion) and the current-asset productivity leg are economically distinct and non-overlapping, and the construction is sign-consistent with broad coverage, though it is a template substitution on a prior composite rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

The numerator already penalizes recent total-liability growth, so the NEG(TREND(lct/cogs)) leg substantially double-counts short-term funding expansion, and the overall form is a one-component swap into the archived Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value template.

Folding both the deficit and the liability-growth penalty into the denominator is a coherent, sign-consistent single-ratio alternative to the two archived adjustments (multiplicative shrinkage rather than subtraction), which is a real structural difference, though the incremental information over the existing deficit-adjusted cash yield may be modest.

This is a single-input substitution (DELTA(che) for oancf) into the archived Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap, and DELTA(che) is a weaker coverage proxy since cash can rise from financing or asset sales, making it partly a rediscovery of the liability-growth/working-capital accrual anomaly.

Multiplying two one-sided truncated legs (whose components are both already in the archive, one of them weak) leaves a large mass of exact zeros so the cross-sectional rank degenerates into ties over most of the universe, making any apparent improvement over the parent trap hard to attribute to the added conditioning.
